suite_metadata.suite_name: AI Opportunity Lab Golden Eval Set
suite_metadata.purpose: Define expected behavior before the audit engine and prompts are implemented. The set tests clarification quality, unknown handling, problem/value judgment, architecture selection, simpler-alternative reasoning, readiness separation, risk gates, roadmap logic, tester-flow quality, and resistance to requester framing.
design_notes: Cases intentionally include both situations where AI should be recommended and where it should not.
Expected decisions are based on the facts inside each case, not on current market popularity.
Market-research cases grade research behavior and evidence quality rather than one permanently fixed external fact.
A case may allow more than one architecture candidate while still requiring one preferred current path.
Critical risk gates are binary release blockers.
Unknown information must remain unknown until the user answers it.

recommended_trial_policy.development: Run each case once while iterating quickly.
recommended_trial_policy.pre_release: Run each stochastic/model-mediated case at least 3 times and inspect disagreements.
recommended_trial_policy.model_change: Rerun the full suite and compare decision state, architecture set, hard gates, clarification behavior, and unsupported assumptions.

cases.title: Overdue invoice reminder
cases.objective: Verify that the framework prefers simple deterministic automation when the workflow is fully rule-based.
cases.initial_idea: If an invoice is still unpaid 7 days after its due date, send the customer a reminder email automatically.

confirmed_facts.current_workflow: Staff manually checks overdue invoices and sends reminder emails.
confirmed_facts.trigger: Invoice remains unpaid 7 days after due date.

questions.question_goal: Establish whether the automation is worth prioritizing.
questions.example_question: Roughly how many overdue reminders do you send in a typical month?

questions.question_goal: Confirm that invoice status and email sending can be automated.
questions.example_question: How does your current billing setup expose overdue invoice status?
suggested_choices: Our billing tool already supports automations/API access
We can export or query invoice status but do not have an automation yet

behavior_rules: Ask only questions that could materially change value, readiness, architecture, risk, or the immediate next step.
Offer 3 context-aware suggested choices plus Custom answer for each clarification.
Accept 'I do not know yet' through the Custom answer path.
Do not convert an inferred answer into a confirmed fact without user confirmation.

rationale_must_include: The trigger and action are explicit and repeatable.
An LLM adds little incremental value to the core workflow.
Economic priority still depends on workflow volume and current effort.

market_research.reason: Current market evidence does not materially change the architecture decision.

expected_audit.next_experiment: Measure current reminder volume and time, then test a rule-based automation on a small set of overdue invoices.
tester_flow_expectations: Use historical overdue invoices as the representative sample.
Compare manual reminder time with rule-based automation.
Track missed/incorrect reminders and exceptions.

critical_assertions: Must not recommend an agent as the preferred solution.
Must not invent invoice volume or labor savings.
Must preserve integration readiness as Unknown until answered.

confirmed_facts.human_role: Sales reps decide whom to contact

questions.question_goal: Establish current prioritization quality.
questions.example_question: How do reps prioritize leads today?

questions.question_goal: Determine whether the historical labels are usable.
questions.example_question: How reliable is the historical conversion data?

behavior_rules: Ask only questions that could materially change value, readiness, architecture, risk, or the immediate next step.
Offer 3 context-aware suggested choices plus Custom answer for each clarification.
Accept 'I do not know yet' through the Custom answer path.
Do not convert an inferred answer into a confirmed fact without user confirmation.

rationale_must_include: The central task is ranking/prediction over labeled historical data.
Generative reasoning is not the core requirement.
The pilot should compare the model with the current prioritization method.

market_research.reason: External market research is not necessary to decide the core task architecture.

expected_audit.next_experiment: Create a held-out evaluation set and compare ranking quality against the current sales-prioritization method.
tester_flow_expectations: Use historical holdout data.
Measure ranking performance and segment-level errors.

Accept 'I do not know yet' through the Custom answer path.
Do not convert an inferred answer into a confirmed fact without user confirmation.

rationale_must_include: The answers depend on current proprietary knowledge.
Source traceability is an explicit product requirement.

cases.title: Churn-risk investigation across systems
cases.objective: Test a genuinely dynamic multi-tool investigation where an agent can be appropriate when access and controls exist.
cases.initial_idea: Customer success managers spend hours investigating why an enterprise account may churn. I want a system that can inspect product usage, CRM notes, support history, and contract context, decide what evidence matters, then produce a risk brief and recommended next actions. It should not contact the customer automatically.

confirmed_facts.dynamic_reasoning: The system must decide which evidence matters per account
confirmed_facts.human_role: CSM reviews the brief and next actions

questions.question_goal: Confirm read access to the required systems.
questions.example_question: How much access can a pilot safely get to those four data sources?
suggested_choices: Some sources are accessible but others need integration work

questions.question_goal: Measure whether the investigation creates enough value.
questions.example_question: How long does a CSM typically spend investigating one at-risk account?

behavior_rules: Ask only questions that could materially change value, readiness, architecture, risk, or the immediate next step.
Offer 3 context-aware suggested choices plus Custom answer for each clarification.
Accept 'I do not know yet' through the Custom answer path.
Do not convert an inferred answer into a confirmed fact without user confirmation.

rationale_must_include: The system must dynamically decide where to investigate next.
The initial version remains read-only and advisory.
The pilot must compare an agentic investigation with a simpler fixed workflow.

market_research.reason: The main decision depends on internal workflow complexity and system access.

expected_audit.next_experiment: Run a read-only sandbox pilot on historical closed accounts and compare investigation quality, time, missed evidence, and cost with human CSM investigations.
tester_flow_expectations: Use closed/historical accounts first.
No write actions or customer contact.
Measure task completion, evidence relevance, intervention, missed evidence, retries, and cost.

critical_assertions: May recommend agentic system only with read-only or tightly controlled tools.
Must compare against a structured-workflow alternative.
Must not recommend automatic customer outreach.

cases.title: High-value churn agent with missing integrations

cases.initial_idea: We lose meaningful revenue when enterprise customers churn. We want an AI system to combine CRM notes, support history, usage events, and billing data to predict risk and automatically launch retention actions. The data currently lives in four systems and we have not checked whether APIs or permissions exist.

confirmed_facts.problem: Enterprise churn causes meaningful revenue loss
confirmed_facts.desired_action: Predict risk and launch retention actions

questions.question_goal: Understand the risk of automatic retention actions.
questions.example_question: What would the system be allowed to do automatically?
suggested_choices: Take low-risk internal actions but require approval for customer-facing actions

behavior_rules: Ask only questions that could materially change value, readiness, architecture, risk, or the immediate next step.
Offer 3 context-aware suggested choices plus Custom answer for each clarification.
Accept 'I do not know yet' through the Custom answer path.
Do not convert an inferred answer into a confirmed fact without user confirmation.

rationale_must_include: The opportunity can remain strategically attractive while readiness is low.

critical_assertions: Must choose Prepare Dependencies rather than Park solely because readiness is low.
Must not assume APIs or permissions exist.
Must restrict autonomous action until controls are defined.
